q: How tight is the 8/pi^2 success-probability floor of BHT'98 Theorem 5 in the small-P regime? Our replication showed empirical P(success) >= 0.87 across all 8 configurations (N=16, t in {1,2,4,8}, P in {16,32}), which is well above the 0.811 analytical floor. Does the floor become tight as P shrinks toward 4 (the theorem's minimum) or as t/N approaches 1/2?
basis: Every measured P(success_emp) column of our 8x1 sweep exceeded 8/pi^2, with the tightest gap being ~0.06 (at t=2, P=32, P_emp=0.871). No configuration got close to the analytical bound, suggesting the proof is loose.
next_steps: Sweep P down to 4-8 and t/N up toward 0.5-eps at N=32 and N=64 with 10^5 shots per point; overlay P_emp against 8/pi^2 and check whether the bound is asymptotically tight or a permanently loose constant. If loose, publish a tighter analytical bound.

q: For what minimum P does the max-probability rounded estimator round(t_tilde) become unbiased for a given (t, N)? Our N=16, t=1, P=32 case still showed a positive bias (t_tilde = 1.348 -> rounds to 1 correctly but the mean estimate is biased high).
basis: For t=1 the true phase f = P*arcsin(1/4)/pi is non-integer, so the QFT concentrates mass on two adjacent bins and the amplitude-weighted mean drifts. We saw t_tilde = 1.348 at P=32 (bias 0.35) and t_tilde = 0.609 at P=16 (bias -0.39, opposite sign).
next_steps: Enumerate the exact post-QFT distribution analytically for small P and t, compute E[t_tilde] and Var[t_tilde] in closed form, then compare to Monte Carlo. Determine the P threshold where mean bias falls below 0.5 for each t/N in {1/16,...,1/2}.

q: How does the fold f_tilde <- min(f_tilde, P - f_tilde) behave at the boundary f = P/2? Our t=8=N/2 case sits exactly at f=P/4 so we never triggered the boundary, but t slightly less than N/2 could see a discontinuous rounding artefact when the amplitude mass straddles P/2.
basis: Our sweep intentionally used t values (1,2,4,8) that give clean f = P*theta/pi and never hit f = P/2. This is a known edge case in phase-estimation folding but the paper's Theorem 5 proof does not visibly analyse it.
next_steps: Run t in {7,15,31} at N in {16,32,64} to probe f near P/2; if the fold creates a systematic gap or double-counting, propose a soft-fold (weighted average of f and P-f).

q: Can catalytic / iterative phase estimation replicate Theorem 5's bound at logarithmically shallower depth? Our transpiled circuits for (P=32, N=16) reached depth ~1800-2400, which is dominated by the singly-controlled Grover chain of length P.
basis: The controlled-Grover chain of length P-1 is the depth bottleneck; textbook 'iterative QPE' or 'Kitaev's algorithm' can achieve the same additive precision with O(log P) qubits and shallower overall depth at the cost of extra classical post-processing.
next_steps: Implement iterative QPE (Kitaev-style, one control qubit reused) on the same GroverOperator, compare depth and empirical P(success). If iterative QPE matches Theorem 5 asymptotically it becomes the preferred NISQ-era counting primitive.

q: Is the algorithm invariant to the choice of marked-set indices, or do certain choices (e.g. all indices sharing a bit) interact badly with the Qiskit DiagonalGate + GroverOperator synthesis to produce sub-optimal transpiled depth or a different empirical bias?
basis: We fixed the marked set to {0, ..., M-1} for reproducibility, which is a highly structured set. The counting output is theoretically invariant under permutations of the domain, but the transpiled circuit is not, and gate synthesis or numerical error could differ.
next_steps: Repeat the M=1,2,4 runs with 10 randomly sampled marked sets each, compare (best_t_hat, P_success_emp, depth) distributions. If depth or bias is a strong function of the marked-set structure that is an actionable finding for benchmark authors.
